record.paper_title: Recent progress and open problems in the Bergman space
record.original_question: Let A^-infinity be the algebra of analytic functions on D satisfying a growth bound |f(z)| <= C(1 - |z|^2)^(-N) for some positive constants C and N. If f belongs to L^2_a(D) and is cyclic in A^-infinity, meaning it generates a dense ideal there, must f also be cyclic in L^2_a(D)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{D}=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z|<1\}$ be the open unit disk. Define:

(a) The Bergman space $L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$ consisting of analytic functions $f:\mathbb{D}\to\mathbb{C}$ with
$$\|f\|^2_{L^2_a}=\int_{\mathbb{D}} |f(z)|^2\,dA(z)<\infty,$$
where $dA$ is normalized area measure. A function $f\in L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$ is called cyclic in $L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$ if the closed subspace generated by $\{z^n f(z):n=0,1,2,\dots\}$ equals $L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$.

(b) The Korenblum algebra
$$A^{-\infty}=\Big\{f\in\mathrm{Hol}(\mathbb{D}):\exists\, C,N>0\text{ such that }|f(z)|\le C(1-|z|^2)^{-N}\text{ for all }z\in\mathbb{D}\Big\},$$
endowed with its natural inductive limit topology. A function $f\in A^{-\infty}$ is called cyclic in $A^{-\infty}$ if the ideal $f\cdot A^{-\infty}$ is dense in $A^{-\infty}$.

It is known that any $f\in L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$ which is cyclic in $L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$ is also cyclic in $A^{-\infty}$.

Question: Does the converse hold? That is, if $f\in L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$ is cyclic in $A^{-\infty}$, must $f$ be cyclic in $L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$?
artifact.status_search_result: This is Korenblum's well-known open problem on the equivalence of cyclicity in $A^{-\infty}$ and in $L^2_a$. Recent surveys (Korenblum's principle for Bergman spaces with radial weights, 2023; Weighted Korenblum-Roberts Theory, 2025) continue to treat related cyclicity questions and Korenblum-Roberts type characterizations; no resolution of the converse implication in this full generality appears to be established. The problem appears still open.

status_evidence.title: Korenblum's principle for Bergman spaces with radial weights
status_evidence.snippet: Cyclicity questions and Korenblum-type principles for Bergman spaces are studied; the equivalence of cyclicity in $L^p_a$ and $A^{-\infty}$ is referenced as a guiding open problem.
status_evidence.claim: Korenblum's cyclicity converse problem remains a central open question in the cyclic vector theory for Bergman spaces.

status_evidence.title: Weighted Korenblum-Roberts Theory
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work extends the Korenblum-Roberts characterization of cyclic singular inner functions, but does not resolve the general $A^{-\infty}$ vs $L^2_a$ cyclicity equivalence.
status_evidence.claim: Recent extensions concern singular inner functions; the general converse for arbitrary $f\in L^2_a$ is not established.

status_evidence.title: The Mathematics of Boris Korenblum: Past, Present, and Future
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses Korenblum's contributions including cyclicity in $A^{-\infty}$ and the connection to $L^2_a$ cyclicity.
status_evidence.claim: The converse cyclicity problem is attributed to Korenblum and remains a guiding question.
